senses.sense_definition: A senior officer in a royal court who manages the domestic affairs of the monarch's household and accounts.

examples.text: The <w>chamberlain</w> organized the grand banquet and ensured that royal protocol was strictly observed.
All expenditures for the palace renovation had to be approved directly by the King's <w>chamberlain</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A high officer of state, such as in certain governments, religious orders, or the Vatican, often holding an honorary or ceremonial title.

examples.text: During the transition period between pontiffs, the papal <w>chamberlain</w> administers the temporal affairs of the Church.
He was appointed as the city's honorary <w>chamberlain</w> during the commemorative celebration.

senses.sense_definition: A senior or trusted servant responsible for managing the rooms in an inn or large house.

examples.text: Upon arriving at the roadside tavern, the weary travelers were shown to their beds by the <w>chamberlain</w>.
The inn's <w>chamberlain</w> took care of the luggage and kept watch over the guests' quarters.

traits.comment: no longer in common use for innkeeping

senses.sense_definition: Neville Chamberlain (1869–1940), the British Prime Minister known for his policy of appeasement prior to World War II.

examples.text: Many historians continue to debate the diplomatic strategies adopted by <w>Chamberlain</w> in 1938.
After signing the Munich Agreement, <w>Chamberlain</w> returned to Britain declaring that he had secured peace.

senses.sense_definition: An English surname derived from the occupational title of chamberlain.

examples.text: Professor <w>Chamberlain</w> delivered an insightful lecture on early modern European history.
